## Design note

Built to bang doors. Front drive, a stiff rear and a plated diff make it dive into corners on the brakes and claw out on the power; lift off and the rear steps out on cue. Slow in a straight line next to the supercars, but it brakes later than the road supercars and shrugs off the contact that ends their night. The cheapest way into a race-built car.

## How this car breaks

A production steel shell with a welded roll cage, seam welding and a steel bumper beam behind the plastic: the toughest race car in the roster, designed for contact. Splitter, wing and plastic bumpers break off on the first touch and are cheap; the transverse engine sits right behind the radiator, so hard frontals still end it.

## Sources (type)

- series homologation sheets for 2010s FWD touring-car racers (minimum weight, boost limit, dimensions)
- team-published dyno figures for homologated 2.0 L turbo engines
- on-board telemetry figures for the class (braking g, cornering g)
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, race caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 589 | 0.80 | 470 |
| pitch | 2285 | 0.88 | 2010 |
| yaw | 2481 | 0.90 | 2230 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.84·W·H = 2.26 m²; Cd = 0.38 → **CdA = 0.859 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = +0.00 / -0.10 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). Add-on aero `aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0.05 F / 0.25 R m² (front splitter and a homologated single-element rear wing (small: touring-car aero is limited by the rules)). Net downforce Cl·A 0.05 F / 0.35 R m² → 120 kg at 250 km/h, 13% front (static weight 63% front).

## Engine

2.0 L DOHC 16-valve I4, single turbo with anti-lag, intercooled, homologated boost limit. Class-typical touring-car 2.0 T under its boost cap (~252 kW at 6500 rpm, 420 N·m plateau) per series homologation data; the cap makes the plateau dead flat from 2500 to 4500.

Peak **252 kW @ 6500 rpm**, **420 N·m @ 2500 rpm**. Idle 1200 / redline 7000 / limiter 7200 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.10 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 12% of peak torque = 50 N·m. Power-to-weight 203 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

6-speed paddle-shift sequential (dog engagement), plated front LSD, sintered race clutch. Layout **FWD**; front diff: clutch LSD, preload 80 N·m, power ramp 0.60, coast ramp 0.35; rear diff: open. Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 670 N·m. Shift time 0.15 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.92 | 9.78 | 87 |
| 2 | 2.06 | 6.90 | 123 |
| 3 | 1.67 | 5.59 | 151 |
| 4 | 1.40 | 4.69 | 180 |
| 5 | 1.20 | 4.02 | 211 |
| 6 | 1.05 | 3.52 | 241 |

Final drive 3.35, reverse 2.80. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.321 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.33 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 370 kg | 2.40 Hz | 84100 N/m | 3680 N·s/m | 5520 N·s/m | 0.08 m |
| Rear | 211 kg | 2.60 Hz | 56300 N/m | 2270 N·s/m | 3400 N·s/m | 0.09 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.2°/g with 45% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.355 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 205928 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 107663 F / 70281 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **0 F / 17200 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.1°/g, front share 49%. Bump stops 250000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -3.5° F / -2.0° R, toe +0.00° F / -0.10° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 36 mm + 32 mm + 30 mm → A = 25.3 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.52: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.52·100 bar·25.3 cm²·0.165 m = **4340 N·m**
- Rear: 278 mm disc, pistons per side 36 mm → A = 10.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 114 mm, pad μ = 0.45: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.45·100 bar·10.2 cm²·0.114 m = **1044 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 4340 / 1044 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.36), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.73 → **3170 / 760 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1553 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.04×), rear needs 393 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.93×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 803 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 3170 N·m front / 760 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1080 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 12.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 11.5 m → outer-front path radius 5.62 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.14 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.574 rad (32.9°)** (outer 28.5°, inner 38.7° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 2.0 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/merlo_20t.json`)

257 nodes, 1620 beams, 8 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id merlo_20t --profile sedan --width 1.95 --length 4.5 --height 1.38 --wheelbase 2.68 --mass 247.6 --car-mass 1237.8 --clearance 0.08 --front-overhang 0.95 --strength 1.15` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 4).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Welded multi-point roll cage tied to the pillars and sills: 341 passenger-cell beams (cabin, sills, pillars, roof rails, cross-members) × 1.60 section.
- Transverse engine: gearbox mounted on the left end of the engine block (gen-lattice places it in the tunnel at the firewall, as for FR).
